subject: Private deployment: snapshot escrow & operator-access proposal
messages:
From: Megan Sanders <megan.sanders@centrata-health.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@centrata-health.com
Date: 2027-11-02T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Snapshot escrow and operator access for on-prem deployment

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and security are starting to line up on our side for the on-prem deployment (private VPC) and we have two asks we need to cover before we move forward with the order form:

1) Escrow-like snapshot policy: we need a documented process for periodic snapshots (encrypted) that we can verify independently in the event of service discontinuation. Our legal team is asking for minimum retention, handover process, and a restoration proof test.

2) Operator access boundary: we need a clear description of what Redwood operator accounts can and cannot do for on-prem — read-only snapshots, emergency console-only access, and audit trails.

I attached our security questionnaire with the initial fields filled. Can you share your proposed language (MSA/Order Form addendum) and a suggested timeline? Procurement would prefer contract-ready wording rather than high-level notes.

Best,
Megan Sanders
Sr. IT Procurement Manager
Centrata Health

Attachments: Centrata_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Sanders <megan.sanders@centrata-health.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-02T12:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot escrow and operator access for on-prem deployment

Megan —

Appreciate the clarity and the questionnaire. Attached is a draft addendum to the MSA and a short outline of our proposed operational controls. Highlights up front so procurement/legal can triage:

- Snapshot escrow model: daily encrypted snapshots (S3) retained for 90 days by default; in the event of customer-initiated termination or defined failure modes, Redwood will make a single final snapshot available to a mutually-agreed trustee (S3 cross-account access) within 7 business days. No IP transfer — snapshot is provided for restoration only; license terms in the MSA remain in force.
- Restoration proof: we can run a test restore to a consensual dev environment and provide logs; propose a one-time restoration test during onboarding and an annual verification on request (paid engineering time).
- Operator access: operator accounts allowed only as time-limited, console-only sessions enforced by our PAM system; all sessions recorded and stored for 180 days; access requires customer approval unless an emergency (incident response) is declared.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 artifacts and an evidence bundle mapping will be included; anything beyond that we can surface via a secured portal or a signed NDA.

I routed this to Legal and Solutions (cc'd) to get redline-ready language back to you within 48 hours. Can we tentatively schedule a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the proposed clauses and the restoration test scope?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_Private_Addendum_PROPOSED.docx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-02T14:00:00-05:00
Subject: Internal: quick legal review requested — Centrata snapshot/ops proposal

Team —

Looping you in. Centrata asked for contract-ready wording for: snapshot escrow-like handover, operator access boundary, and restoration proof. I attached our proposed addendum. Key redline asks from customer and proposed positions below — please confirm acceptability or propose language changes:

1) License scope / IP: Customer wants explicit language that snapshot handover does not grant rights to use Redwood IP beyond restoration. Proposed: "Snapshot delivery is solely for restoration to Customer-controlled environments; no license to Redwood model weights or runtime is granted."

2) Trustee flow: Customer prefers a neutral trustee escrow. Proposed: cross-account S3 access via trustee OR escrow agent; Redwood to provide audit logs of transfer.

3) Restoration test: Customer requests proof of restoration. Proposed: one onboarding test included; additional tests billable per engineering rate. Need legal to confirm this is commercially OK.

4) Operator access: limit to console-only, time-limited sessions with MFA and recording; require explicit customer pre-approval for non-emergency sessions.

5) Holdback / indemnity: customer asked for a limited holdback clause tied to evidence delivery. We should keep any financial holds minimal; legal input on acceptable language needed.

I've created a REDLINE version (attached) with inline comments. If we can sign off on the core principles, I can send the redline back to Megan and procurement today.

Thanks — Hannah

Attachments: MSA_Private_Addendum_REDLINE.docx

From: Megan Sanders <megan.sanders@centrata-health.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@centrata-health.com
Date: 2027-11-03T08:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot escrow and operator access for on-prem deployment

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A few clarifications from procurement/security after an internal review:

- Restoration proof: instead of an annual "on request" test, they want documented acceptance criteria for the one-time restoration test plus a signed certificate of completion. Is that feasible?
- Trustee: Centrata prefers a neutral third-party escrow agent for the final snapshot transfer rather than cross-account access. Can Redwood work with an escrow agent we name?
- Order Form: Please confirm whether the addendum applies to dedicated capacity subscriptions or only to the private VPC/on-prem SKU; procurement needs a DocuSign-ready order form showing pricing difference.

If you can take the redline and produce a DocuSign-ready order form (Schedule B showing Private Deployment fees and an appendix for the snapshot process), procurement can move to PO issuance within 10 business days.

Also attached: a short PDF with their procurement notes.

Best,
Megan

Attachments: Centrata_Security_Notes.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-03T10:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick legal review requested — Centrata snapshot/ops proposal

Hannah/Team —

Reviewed the REDLINE. Legal is generally comfortable with the proposed structure with the following updates (inline language included in attached final Schedule B):

- Snapshot delivery: acceptable with explicit non-transfer clause. Suggested language: "Delivery of encrypted snapshot media is for Customer restoration purposes only; Customer shall not use the snapshot to access or replicate Redwood proprietary model binaries, weights, or runtime artifacts beyond restoration for Customer-owned data."
- Trustee: we can accept a customer-nominated escrow agent provided the agent signs our standard escrow engagement and confidentiality addenda. We will not do direct cross-account granting to avoid entitlement drift.
- Restoration test: convert to "one onboarding restoration test with defined acceptance criteria and signed certificate of completion." Additional tests can be performed for a commercially reasonable fee; add rate card appendix.
- Operator access: add explicit emergency definition and require documented authorization flow; keep session recording retention at 180 days but remove any unlimited retention language.

I have prepared a DocuSign-ready Order Form Schedule B and a final appendix (OrderForm_ScheduleB_FINAL.docx) that incorporates these points. Please review quickly; if accepted we can send to Megan with the DocuSign link.

I'll handle the legal sign-off on the escrow engagement once we have the escrow agent details from the customer.

Thanks — Laura
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_ScheduleB_FINAL.docx
